guidance: A materials count, not a design. Nothing here says whether a barrier will hold back water at a site, and a temporary sandbag wall can fail or be overtopped, so follow local flood-fighting guidance and emergency instructions. Filled bag sizes and weights are typical trade figures, not a product specification, and the wall is counted as one bag thick.
method: Bags along one course is the barrier length divided by the filled bag length and rounded up: ceil(length / 20 in) for a standard bag, 16 in for a small bag and 24 in for a heavy bag, with the bags laid end to end. Courses is the height divided by the filled bag thickness, 6, 5 or 8 in, rounded up. The wall total is bags per course times courses for a wall one bag thick. The spare is the chosen whole percentage of the wall total, rounded up, and covers split bags and the half-bag offsets at the ends. Sand weight is the total bags times the trade weight of a filled bag, 35 lb standard, 25 lb small, 50 lb heavy, converted to kilograms at 0.45359237 kg per lb and to volume at 100 lb of dry sand per cubic foot and 27 cubic feet per cubic yard. Wall face is length times height in square feet, converted at 0.09290304 m2 per ft2, and bags per square foot of face is the wall total divided by that area, shown to one decimal because it is a rough rate. Lengths convert at 12 in per foot and 39.37007874015748 in per metre; heights at 1 in per inch and 0.3937007874015748 in per centimetre. Inputs are a length from 1 to 500 ft or 0.5 to 150 m with at most two decimals, a height from 6 to 120 in or 15 to 300 cm with at most two decimals, one of three bag sizes and a spare allowance from 0 to 50 whole percent. Bag counts round up; sand and area figures round half up at the displayed decimals. Everything runs in the browser with no uploads, storage or network calls.
